chapter: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants
question_text: Name the three basic tissue systems in flowering plants. Give the tissue names under each system.

page_header: Histology and Anatomy of Flowering Plants · 4 marks

steps.label: The three tissue systems
steps.margin_note: One mark for the three names alone. Write them as a numbered list.
lines: On the basis of their position in the plant
body, the tissues of a flowering plant are
grouped into three tissue systems:
1. Epidermal tissue system
2. Ground tissue system
3. Vascular tissue system
steps.why: The grouping is by position, so the three names already run from the outside of the plant inward. Getting that order right stops you from putting a tissue in the wrong system later.
common_mistakes: Writing epidermis, cortex and stele. Those are regions of one organ, not tissue systems.
Naming only two systems. There are three.
steps.memory_tip: Outside, middle, inside: epidermal, ground, vascular.

steps.label: Epidermal tissue system
steps.margin_note: Name the system, then list what is under it. One line for the job it does.
lines: It forms the outermost covering of the whole
plant body.
Tissues under it: the epidermis, the stomata
set in it, and the epidermal appendages, that
is trichomes on the shoot and root hairs on
the root.
It protects the plant and controls the loss of
water.
steps.why: This system is defined by being on the outside, so everything that sits in or grows out of the outermost layer belongs to it.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the stomata and the hairs. The question asks for the tissues under each system.
Calling the cuticle a tissue. It is a waxy layer, not a tissue.
steps.memory_tip: Everything on the surface: epidermis, stomata, trichomes, root hairs.

steps.label: Ground tissue system
steps.margin_note: Four tissue names, then the three cell types that build them.
lines: It is all the tissue lying between the
epidermal system and the vascular bundles.
Tissues under it: cortex, pericycle, pith
(medulla) and medullary rays.
These are made of parenchyma, collenchyma and
sclerenchyma.
steps.why: This system is defined by what it is not: everything that is neither the covering nor the conducting tissue. That is why it is the largest of the three.
common_mistakes: Forgetting the medullary rays. They are part of the ground tissue system.
Putting the xylem or phloem here. They belong to the vascular system.
steps.memory_tip: Ground tissue is the filling: cortex, pericycle, pith and rays.

steps.label: Vascular tissue system
steps.margin_note: Close with the three system names in order so the answer ends where it started.
lines: It is the conducting system of the plant,
present in the form of vascular bundles.
Tissues under it: xylem and phloem.
Xylem carries water and minerals upward;
phloem carries food.
steps.why: Only two tissues make up this system, so the mark is really for naming xylem and phloem and saying what each carries.
common_mistakes: Writing cambium as a third tissue of this system. Cambium is a meristem.
Swapping the two jobs. Xylem carries water, phloem carries food.
steps.memory_tip: Two tissues only: xylem for water, phloem for food.

insider_note: The question has two halves, name and list. A student who names the three systems and stops loses three of the four marks.
